intro: Monday June 22. First full US session post-3-day closure. Key verdict: the Sunday futures optimism did NOT fully translate — SPX opened 56–69 pts below futures (7,487–7,500 vs 7,556), VIX borderline (16.78 intraday, opened 17.04), and DXY held at 100.76 (gate NOT cleared). The post-FOMC Week 2 pattern is partially active. The framework pivots to June 23 for the DXY gate attempt and June 24 for the override event (Micron Q3 + NVDA Annual Meeting on the same day — EPS $19.95 est., revenue $34.66B est., gross margin >80%, 27 analysts Strong Buy). Two tactical developments from June 22: (A) SPCX gap-up on IG ratings to ~$185 has activated Day 1 of the two-consecutive-close re-entry watch — June 23 close above $185 would unlock re-entry; (B) BTC June 22 UTC candle is tracking above the $63,500 stop level at $64,117 (11:01 UTC), with stop clock reset probable at UTC midnight. The ideas below are calibrated for the June 23 session — the last session before the week's primary event. Three scenarios for June 23: (A) DXY closes below 100 + IBIT shows net inflow + SPCX Day 2 close above $185 → execute all conditional adds simultaneously; (B) DXY holds above 100 but macro is stable → hold unchanged and arrive positioned for June 24 pre-open; (C) 30Y breaks above 5.00% or IBIT shows resumed outflows → reduce high-multiple exposures ahead of June 24 uncertainty.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: DXY gate failed June 22 (100.76 vs <100 required); June 23 is the next gate attempt; June 24 Annual Meeting + Micron Q3 is the override catalyst 48 hours away — add before the open regardless of gate status.
ideas.why: NVDA's 50-DMA at ~$206.74 held as intraday support on June 22 (session low $206.50) with elevated volume (241M vs 161.7M avg) — the technical and institutional evidence is unambiguously constructive for the near-term thesis. The conditional add gate (DXY <100.00) failed on June 22 (DXY settled 100.76), but the Annual Meeting override rule is now 48 hours away: Jensen Huang speaks at the NVDA Annual Meeting on June 24 (9 AM PT) on the SAME day Micron reports Q3 earnings (EPS $19.95 est., revenue $34.66B est., gross margin >80% expected). The compound signal of confirmed AI demand (MU HBM revenue) + confirmed management conviction (Jensen AI capex commentary) on the same trading day is the most powerful single-day catalyst available in the AI semiconductor sector. Elevated June 22 volume signals institutions are already positioning ahead of June 24.
ideas.trigger: June 23 session close: if DXY closes below 100.00 AND VIX stays below 17 → execute $205–$215 add immediately at confirmed-gate close. OVERRIDE TRIGGER (regardless of DXY): pre-June-24-open add (before 9 AM PT) — Jensen Annual Meeting is the override catalyst; arrive fully positioned BEFORE the Annual Meeting, not at the open. Do not wait for a DXY confirmation that may not arrive before June 24.
ideas.risk: DXY holds above 100 through June 24 (Warsh hawkish Fed speech on June 22–23 reverses weekend FX improvement); Micron Q3 misses the elevated $34.66B / $19.95 EPS / >80% gross margin bar; 30Y yield breaks above 5.00% before June 24 open.

ideas.name: Micron Technology
ideas.idea: June 24 Q3 earnings — EPS $19.95 est. / revenue $34.66B est. / gross margin >80% expected; HBM sold-out through 2026–2027; 27 analysts Strong Buy; elevated bar means beat-and-raise is the consensus expectation, not the upside scenario.
ideas.why: Micron Q3 consensus has been revised up 3.1% in 30 days (revenue $34.52B → $34.66B; EPS $19.72 → $19.95) with gross margin expectations now breaking 80% — levels that would be new records for Micron. HBM capacity is confirmed sold-out through 2026 into early 2027 by multiple industry sources. This is not a speculative consensus — it is a consensus built on disclosed supply agreements and customer order books. A June 24 MU beat-and-raise simultaneously validates NVDA's Blackwell/Vera Rubin HBM supply chain, triggers a SK Hynix gap-up on June 25 KOSPI, and accelerates BTC's risk-appetite recovery. Micron is the most direct US-listed proxy for AI memory demand, with 21% global HBM market share (vs SK Hynix 58%).
ideas.trigger: Pre-earnings entry: buy MU at $95–$110 on June 23 session before June 24 results. Post-earnings on June 24: if MU beats revenue ($34.66B) AND guides above consensus on HBM for Q4 2026 → hold for post-earnings momentum leg (target $115–$125). If MU misses or guides down on HBM → exit immediately and reduce NVDA/SK Hynix exposure.
ideas.risk: MU misses the elevated $34.66B / $19.95 EPS / >80% gross margin triple bar; management warns on Q4 2026 HBM demand from enterprise budget pressure (AI spending slowdown signal); Samsung gains HBM market share faster than consensus models.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: June 25 KST KOSPI session is the primary Micron Q3 read-through event — hold positioned before June 23 KST close; gap above ₩2,891,000 ATH is the base case on a Micron beat.
ideas.why: SK Hynix holds 58% of the global HBM market. When Micron confirms HBM sold-out through 2026–2027 (consensus on June 24), the direct read-through for SK Hynix's HBM4E pricing power and production margin is the clearest AI memory validation in the company's history. The June 25 KST KOSPI open is the first session for Korean buy-side to react to Micron's June 24 results. A Micron beat-and-raise on HBM ASPs and volume, combined with confirmation of sold-out capacity through 2027, is a direct ₩3,000,000+ catalyst for SK Hynix on June 25 KST. Additionally: Seoul Economic Daily June 22 confirms ADR process proceeding normally (SEC clearance expected late June, listing July–August 2026, $66B total shareholder return including $14B ADR raise). All 38 sell-side analysts remain below current price — PT revision cascade is mandatory and imminent.
ideas.trigger: Hold core long through July 29 Q2 earnings. Tactical: arrive fully positioned before June 23 KST KOSPI close (00:00–06:30 UTC June 23) to be in position for the June 25 KST Micron read-through gap-up. If ADR SEC clearance is announced before June 25 KST: add at market immediately on first KOSPI session after announcement. Stop: ₩2,540,000 (two daily closes below required).
ideas.risk: Micron Q3 miss on HBM demand (especially ASP guidance or Q4 2026 volume outlook) — direct negative read-through for SK Hynix on June 25 KST; ADR SEC clearance delayed beyond June (removes imminent-timeline catalyst); Samsung HBM4E customer qualification ahead of SK Hynix at NVIDIA.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: June 22 UTC Day 2 stop clock in progress: current $64,117, High $64,825 — stop reset probable at UTC midnight (8pm ET); monitor IBIT flow + DXY for size-up conditions.
ideas.why: BTC June 22 UTC candle (Crypto.com MCP, 11:01 UTC) opened at the June 21 clearing level ($63,319, just $46 above June 21 session low $63,273), rallied immediately to $64,825 (session high), and has settled at $64,117 — $617 above the $63,500 stop level. This is the pattern of institutional absorption after a stop-hunt: the June 21 afternoon UTC sell-off cleared overlevered longs; the June 22 UTC session opened at the clearing level and recovered immediately. Two-consecutive-close rule: one Day 1 does not execute the stop; the stop executes ONLY if Day 2 also closes below $63,500. Current trajectory makes Day 2 reset probable. The double-bottom ($62,255–$62,313) was never tested even at the Day 2 UTC open — structural support is intact.
ideas.trigger: June 22 UTC midnight (8pm ET): if close above $63,500 → stop clock RESETS; SIZE-UP conditions for add on June 23: (1) IBIT June 22 flow shows net inflows (farside.co.uk by 7am ET June 23); (2) DXY closes below 100.00 on June 22 or 23; (3) BTC UTC close above $63,500 (confirmed reset). All three → add 25% at $63,500–$65,000. Active stop: $63,500 UTC daily close.
ideas.risk: June 22 US afternoon session (14:00–20:00 UTC) repeats June 21 sell-off pattern (same time window); IBIT shows resumed outflows on June 22 first post-Juneteenth print; DXY reversal above 101 compounds the 'no macro gate clearance' scenario.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: IG ratings gap-up to ~$185 has activated Day 1 close watch; if June 22 closes above $185 on above-average volume → Day 1 confirmed; June 23 close above $185 → RE-ENTRY UNLOCKED.
ideas.why: SPCX gapped from $174.90 (June 18 stop-trigger close) to approximately $185 intraday on June 22, pricing in the 72-hour-unpriced investment-grade ratings (S&P BBB, Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+). The Moody's Baa1 (above Tesla's Baa3) is the single most significant franchise quality signal since the IPO. June 22 is Day 1 of the two-consecutive-close re-entry sequence — if the June 22 DAILY CLOSE is above $185, the framework transitions from 'step aside' to 'Day 1 confirmed, watching for Day 2.' June 24 risk-on backdrop (NVDA Annual Meeting + Micron Q3) would provide the macro support needed for SPCX to hold above $185 for a June 23 Day 2 close confirmation.
ideas.trigger: June 22 DAILY CLOSE above $185 on above-average volume (>100M shares) → Day 1 confirmed; set alert for June 23 close above $185; June 23 close above $185 on above-average volume → RE-ENTRY: buy at market with July $175 put hedge, stop $165 daily close. DO NOT re-enter on June 22 intraday data alone.
ideas.risk: June 22 closes below $185 despite intraday trading above (failed gap-up → 'equity disagrees with rating agencies' confirmed → step aside indefinitely); VIX re-spikes above 18 on June 23 reversal, breaking the post-IG recovery narrative; 84x revenue valuation unchanged — institutional reallocation to new positions limited without a confirmed two-close sequence.

ideas.name: Meta Platforms
ideas.idea: Best post-FOMC recovery vehicle in megacap — self-funded AI, lowest multiple in Mag-7 post-selloff; June 23 DXY gate attempt is the entry confirmation event.
ideas.why: Meta fell -5.44% on June 17 FOMC day — the largest single-session FOMC loss in the Magnificent-7 cohort. At ~$548, Meta's fundamentals remain the cleanest in big tech: AI capex funded entirely from operations, no external debt, international advertising revenue that benefits from DXY declining, and the lowest forward multiple in the Mag-7 post-selloff. June 22's SPX underperforming Sunday futures by 62 pts (7,487 vs 7,556) slightly reduces the setup quality versus the pure risk-on Sunday scenario, but VIX at ~16.78 and DXY at 100.76 (improving) remain constructive. If DXY clears <100 on June 23, Meta is the first capital destination in megacap — less rate-sensitive than NVDA (no gate required), more liquid than SK Hynix, and the most directly torqued to international ad revenue from a DXY decline.
ideas.trigger: June 23: VIX stays below 17 (confirmed at June 23 open) AND DXY shows further decline toward 100 → hold current entry or add at $545–$560, stop $530 daily close. June 24 dual catalyst (Micron + NVDA Annual Meeting) confirming AI capex durability → raise META conviction to medium-high and extend hold. SPX close above 7,500 on June 23 = secondary confirmation.
ideas.risk: DXY reverses above 101 on June 23 open (removes international ad revenue tailwind); 30Y tests 5.00% before June 23 close (multiple compression for long-duration growth across Mag-7); AI regulatory headlines (antitrust, EU data privacy) create specific META headwind separate from the macro environment.

ideas.name: Alphabet
ideas.idea: Cheapest AI monetization in Mag-7 post-FOMC selloff; TPU inference cost advantage; secondary beneficiary of June 24 AI capex confirmation.
ideas.why: Alphabet at ~$355 post-FOMC selloff is the lowest-valued full-stack AI play in the megacap cohort. TPU-driven inference cost leadership gives Google Cloud a structural pricing moat for enterprise AI workloads. If Micron's June 24 beat-and-raise confirms AI memory demand is intact through 2027, it re-rates the entire AI monetization cohort — with GOOGL as the lowest-multiple beneficiary. The Google AI Overviews data through Q1 2026 shows session length extending (not falling), validating the search-moat-extension thesis over the search-cannibalization-risk bear case. Low conviction because SPX underperforming Sunday futures by 62 pts on June 22 reduces the urgency of adding before June 24.
ideas.trigger: June 23 VIX below 17 AND GOOGL holding $348–$352 support → buy at $350–$360, stop $345 daily close. If June 24 Micron + NVDA catalysts deliver positive outcomes → raise conviction to medium and extend hold toward July earnings.
ideas.risk: Antitrust remedies (DOJ search ruling) fracture the advertising-bundle thesis; AI Overviews prove to be a session-length headwind rather than extension (Q2 2026 data shows decline); DXY reversal above 101 reduces international revenue expectations.

ideas.name: SPDR Energy Select Sector ETF
ideas.idea: Iran Hormuz reopening on 30-day timeline; Brent $80.59 structurally below H2 energy equity model assumptions ($87–$90); H2 estimate cuts not yet in consensus.
ideas.why: The Iran ceasefire remains in effect; Hormuz mine-clearance timeline is tracking (30 days). Brent at $80.59 is $6–9 below the embedded H2 2026 assumptions in sell-side energy equity models ($87–$90) — analysts have NOT yet revised H2 estimates to reflect Brent at $80. The disconnect creates a structural short setup: as H2 2026 earnings guidance comes in below consensus over the next 4–6 weeks, XLE estimates get cut sequentially. June 22 SPX underperformance vs futures is slightly supportive for XLE as a defensive short hedge — if post-FOMC Week 2 weakness continues on June 23, risk-off positioning benefits XLE on the short as well. DXY at 100.76 (above 100) is a mild commodity headwind that compounds the supply-side Hormuz pressure.
ideas.trigger: June 23: if XLE opens at $53–$56 with Brent below $83 → initiate or add to short. Any Brent bounce to $82–$84 on Hormuz mine-clearance delay headlines is the premium short entry. Cover only if two consecutive Brent closes above $90 (Hormuz supply addition fails completely).
ideas.risk: Iran ceasefire collapses; Hormuz mine-clearance delayed beyond 60 days; OPEC+ emergency production cut; Brent spike above $90 on a non-Hormuz supply shock (Libya, Nigeria).
